exercises.title: Welcome: learn the workflow
exercises.hint: This introduction is already complete. In watch mode, open the displayed file, then press `n` to continue to the first coding exercise.

exercises.title: Hello: fix the type error
exercises.hint: The function is declared to return Int, but the body returns a String. Replace the string with an integer literal.

exercises.title: Add: make the test pass
exercises.hint: Implement `add` so that `add(2, 3)` returns 5.

exercises.title: Sum to n: a loop
exercises.hint: Use a `for i = 1; i <= n; i = i + 1` loop and a mutable `total` that accumulates each `i`.

exercises.title: Factorial: recursion
exercises.hint: Return `1` when `n <= 1`, otherwise `n * factorial(n - 1)`.

exercises.title: Rectangle area: structs
exercises.hint: The area is `rect.width * rect.height`.

exercises.title: Shape area: enums and match
exercises.hint: Match on `Circle(r)` and `Square(s)`. Use `3 * r * r` for the circle (a stand-in for pi) and `s * s` for the square.

exercises.title: Describe an option: Option and match
exercises.hint: Match on `Some(value)` and `None`. For `Some` return `"some: \{value}"`.

exercises.title: Safe divide: error handling
exercises.hint: Return `Err("division by zero")` when `b == 0`, otherwise `Ok(a / b)`.

exercises.title: Maximum: generics
exercises.hint: Return `a` when `a > b`, otherwise `b`. The `Compare` bound already lets you use `>`.

exercises.title: Speak: traits
exercises.hint: Make `Dog::speak` return "woof" and `Cat::speak` return "meow".

exercises.title: Map: higher-order functions
exercises.hint: Build a fresh array, iterate over `arr`, and push `f(x)` for each element.

exercises.title: Count evens: an array loop
exercises.hint: Iterate over `arr` and count elements where `x % 2 == 0`.

exercises.title: Greeting: string interpolation
exercises.hint: Return `"Hello, \{name}!"` so the supplied name appears in the greeting.

exercises.title: Code point count: Unicode iteration
exercises.hint: `text.length()` counts UTF-16 code units, so an emoji counts as two. Iterate over `text.iter()` and count each Unicode code point (`Char`) instead.

exercises.title: Redact digits: text processing
exercises.hint: Create a `StringBuilder`, iterate over `text.iter()`, write `'*'` for each `char.is_ascii_digit()` and otherwise write the original char, then call `to_string()`.

exercises.title: Score lookup: hash maps
exercises.hint: Build a `@hashmap.HashMap` from `scores`, then return `map.get(name)`. Missing keys return `None`.

exercises.title: Unique count: hash sets
exercises.hint: Create an empty `@hashset.HashSet[Int]`, add each number in `values`, then return `set.length()`.

exercises.title: Word frequencies: update a hash map
exercises.hint: For each word, read its current count with `counts.get(word).unwrap_or(0)`, then store that count plus one with `counts.set(word, ...)`.

exercises.title: Activity summary: review
exercises.hint: Track online names in a `@hashset.HashSet[String]`. Match each event: join adds a name, leave removes it, and a message counts only when its sender is online. Return the set length and message count.

exercises.title: First even: finding an optional value
exercises.hint: Visit the numbers in order. Return `Some(value)` for the first even number; if the loop finishes without one, return `None`.

exercises.title: Double an option: map
exercises.hint: Use `value.map(x => x * 2)`. It changes `Some(x)` and keeps `None` as `None`.

exercises.title: Add options: bind and map
exercises.hint: Use `left.bind(a => right.map(b => a + b))` so either missing value makes the result `None`.

exercises.title: Raise a typed error
exercises.hint: When `value < 0`, use `raise NegativeValue(value)` so callers receive the invalid value in the error.

exercises.title: Catch an error and use a fallback
exercises.hint: Call `checked_divide(a, b)` and handle `DivisionByZero` with `catch { DivisionByZero => fallback }`. Successful division should return unchanged.

exercises.title: Convert a raised error to Result
exercises.hint: Wrap successful division with `Ok(checked_divide(a, b))`, then use `catch { error => Err(error) }` for a raised error.
